title: Native ordinary tensor reindexing on K-flat models
statement: Fix a prime l and a scheme isomorphism g:X≅Y, with l invertible in every residue field on X and Y. Let R,S be native locally finite adic realizations, let A:At(l,X,R), C:At(l,Y,S), and let B:RingReindex(l,X,g,R,S) be function-normalized [def-sf-native-adic-reindexing-data]. There exists ReindexTensor(l,X,g,A,C,B) [def-sf-native-adic-tensor-reindexing]: a cochain total-tensor comparison with the homogeneous pure-tensor formula, preservation of the supplied K-flat tests, its derived comparison with the prescribed representative equation, and the coefficient-unit comparison fixed on sections. This is about ambient ordinary modules and asserts no common-stage realization coherence.

source.place: BS Remark 6.8.15; HRS Lemma 7.9; explicit subargument of lem-sf-adic-reindexing-core, not a verbatim statement of either source.

proof.text: Use the proved homogeneous-section-normalized cochain tensor comparison. Construct an equivalence on ordinary modules from the sectionwise site equivalence and the inverse scalar isomorphism; its induced cochain functor is an equivalence.

For any acyclic test complex N on X, take a preimage Nprime under the cochain equivalence. Faithful exact module reindexing reflects acyclicity, hence Nprime is acyclic. The K-flat hypothesis on P makes totalTensor(Nprime,P) acyclic; exact reindexing preserves that acyclicity. Transport along the cochain tensor comparison and the preimage isomorphism to totalTensor(N,F(P)). This proves every K-flat test.

Use the existing independent-coefficient K-flat resolutions to make restriction to K-flat representatives fully faithful on the product derived category. Apply tensorComparisonDescent to the supplied model comparisons C.models and A.models and the exact-derived factorization. Its representative-square conclusion is definitionally the required reindexTensorRepresentative equation.

The canonical unitToPushforwardObjUnit map is invertible: forget to sheaves of additive groups and check the inverse scalar isomorphism componentwise. Invert it, then apply the degree-zero single-complex comparison. The hom-inverse identities compute its sections as B.iso.hom. The single-complex evaluation isomorphisms give precisely reindexUnitSections. Assemble all seven fields of ReindexTensor.

proof_origin.place: BS Remark 6.8.15; native normalized cochain comparison, transport of acyclic tests through the exact equivalence, representative descent, and direct coefficient-unit construction.

theorem exists_tensor_reindexing_models {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ≅ Y)
    (R : LocallyFiniteAdicRealization.Realization l X)
    (S : LocallyFiniteAdicRealization.Realization l Y)
    [∀ x : X, Invertible (l : X.residueField x)]
    [∀ y : Y, Invertible (l : Y.residueField y)]
    (A : At l X R) (C : At l Y S) (B : RingReindex l X g.hom R S) :
    Nonempty (ReindexTensor l X g.hom A C B)
